findings.title: Manufacturing method claim is performed out of sight and avoided by a different process
findings.attack: Claim 4 ('shape-setting (512) the seat ring in a fixture that holds the load-converting geometry') is avoided by cold-forming the convolution, a polymer ring ([0207]) or a stamped slotted sleeve ([0262]); where shape-setting is used it happens at a supplier, usually abroad, and leaves no reliable signature in the ring. Design-around resistance 3, detectability 2.
findings.least_narrowing_action: No amendment; keep the claim but place enforcement weight on claim 3's structural dependents (62-69, 71-73).

assumptions.text: A1. Scores are relative 1-10 judgements against the saved prior-art set only, not probabilities and not the grant-likelihood score.
A2. Commercial relevance assumes the principal-embodiment core sold as a replacement core and in Presta-pattern valves; no market data in the package.
A3. EPO 'suitable for' reading of purpose and use features in product claims assumed as general practice.
A4. Product-by-process protection (Art. 64(2) EPC, UK s60(1)(c), 35 U.S.C. 271(g)) stated as general practice, not legal opinion.

open_questions.text: Q1. Requester: which product forms carry the revenue (replacement cores, complete valves, spare seat rings, factory-fitted tubes or wheels)?
Q2. Counsel: re-score novelty and inventive-step resilience for claims 1 and 3 after a professional prior-art search.
